entities.summary: Charles François de Broglie, Marquis of Ruffec, was a French soldier and diplomat from the House of Broglie, who played a crucial role in the Seven Years' War (1756-1763) and the French Enlightenment. Born in Paris on August 19, 1719, he served as a military officer under Frederick the Great and later became a key advisor to the French king, Louis XV. De Broglie's diplomatic efforts helped establish the Treaty of Paris (1763), which ended the war and marked a significant turning point in European history. His influence extended beyond his military and diplomatic career, as he was a prominent figure in the French Enlightenment, contributing to the development of liberal thought and the emergence of the French bourgeoisie. De Broglie's legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the French monarchy and the role of the nobility in European politics. His impact on the development of liberal thought and the emergence of the French bourgeoisie is still studied by historians today.
